title: Unfreeze the Plan 2 student loan repayment threshold
headline: Unfreeze the Plan 2 repayment threshold from April 2027. Costs £0.4bn in 2029-30.
description: Budget 2025 froze the repayment threshold for Plan 2 student loans (undergraduates from 2012 to 2022) at its 2026-27 level for three years from April 2027, so graduates start repaying at a lower real income and repay more. The Treasury scored the freeze at £5.9 billion in 2026-27, when the loan book was revalued, then £255 million to £380 million a year. Switch this on to let the threshold rise again from April 2027, giving up the Treasury's costing from that year; the 2026-27 revaluation falls before your Budget and is not undone.

baselinePolicy.text: The Plan 2 repayment threshold is held at its 2026-27 level until April 2030, when it rises with inflation again; the freeze is scored at £285m, £5,915m, £255m, £290m, £355m and £380m from 2025-26 to 2030-31 (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 line 48).

source.quote: This measure maintains the repayment threshold for plan 2 student loans at its financial year 26-27 level until April 2030, when it will increase annually by inflation.

alreadyIncludes: The Plan 2 threshold freeze from 6 April 2027 for three years (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 line 48).

lines.title: Student Loans: Freeze Plan 2 repayment threshold for three years from 6 April 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal on the spending side: the Treasury's costing with the sign kept (the freeze reduced borrowing; ending it costs the same amount). Student loan repayments score as spending in the public finances, which is why the scorecard types the line as Spend.

caveats: The £5.9 billion in 2026-27 is the one-off effect of revaluing the loan book when the freeze was announced; it falls before the earliest start year here and is not applied, so what you see is the running cost of a higher threshold from 2027-28.

The Treasury names student loan repayment forecasts as inherently uncertain: borrower earnings, inflation and household income all move them. The costing is on the OBR November 2025 forecast, not the March 2026 baseline used here.
The scorecard line is the freeze from April 2027; the pre-freeze uprating rule the threshold returns to is the one in the Treasury's pre-measure baseline, which the costing note does not spell out.

considerations.text: The Treasury's scorecard figure is the certified costing, estimated by applying the pre- and post-measure thresholds to Plan 2 borrowers' predicted earnings from Student Loans Company and HMRC data, uprated with the OBR's earnings forecast.

The freeze falls on undergraduates who studied between 2012 and 2022 and earn above the threshold or are expected to by 2027-28 to 2029-30: graduates in their late twenties and thirties, who repay 9% of income above it. Unfreezing gives that back, most to those just above the threshold.
